official.deadline_note: The Ministry of Education publishes no programme-wide deadline; each participating university sets its own window per intake. NCU's online application for the Spring 2027 semester ran 1 August to 30 September 2026 (enrolment 1 February 2027); NTUT's 2027 Fall intake sets a student nomination deadline of 10 March 2027, with results in June 2027 and a September 2027 start. All dates GMT+8.
official.application_cycle: Running since the 2024 academic year (plan period 1 January 2024 to 31 July 2027); Spring and Fall intakes every year
official.status_note: MOE operates no central application, so whether a window is open depends on the university. As of 10 October 2026, NCU's Spring 2027 online window (which closed on 30 September 2026) has ended, while NTUT lists a 2027 Fall intake with a student nomination deadline of 10 March 2027 and states that admitting departments, quotas, funding amounts and eligibility criteria are subject to change based on the latest MOE and NTUT announcements.
official.tuition_coverage_note: MOE states: 'The Taiwanese government covers tuition fees and other administrative costs for up to two years.' MOE's Chinese plan page states the government (National Development Fund) award comprises a one-off air ticket and administrative expenses, a first-year tuition and miscellaneous-fee subsidy, and a second-year tuition and miscellaneous-fee subsidy awarded on merit. NTU's own INTENSE terms cap the tuition and miscellaneous-fee subsidy at NT$50,000 per semester and NT$100,000 per year.
official.funding_period: per month, minimum, for up to 2 years
benefits: Government (National Development Fund) award: a one-off air ticket and administrative expenses, a first-year tuition and miscellaneous-fee subsidy, and a second-year tuition and miscellaneous-fee subsidy awarded on merit.
Participating companies provide each student with a living allowance of at least NT$10,000 per month, for up to two years.
An internship allowance during the off-campus internship course period, at a level not lower than the statutory minimum wage.
Paid off-campus internships during the study period, with the school and the enterprise jointly planning enrolment and course arrangements.
After the work obligation is fulfilled, students may choose to remain in Taiwan to work or return to their home country to work.
eligibility: International students who have completed their second or third year at an overseas university, or junior college graduates and bachelor's degree holders; MOE's Chinese plan page also lists master's degree graduates.
Must be recruited by a participating university into an approved INTENSE programme in a key industry field - STEM, finance or semiconductors.
Some programmes restrict eligible nationalities: NCU's Advanced Mechanical Engineering Programme names Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand.
Must satisfy the participating university's own admission requirements, including its language proficiency minima.

Students who fall under the restrictions of the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan must submit the additional nationality and renunciation documents required by the university.
requirements: Follow the two-year learning and internship plan designed jointly by the university and the partner company.
Accept the obligation to stay in Taiwan and work with the participating company after graduation, for a period matching the number of years of funding received.

At NTU, second-year continued funding requires passing the school's and the partner company's review of grades and performance, plus TOCFL Level A2 or above (English-taught) or TOCFL Level B1 or above (Chinese-taught) in listening and reading.
Complete the application online and upload all documents before the deadline; NCU does not accept hard-copy, late or incomplete applications.
documents: Official degree certificate of the highest degree completed, with a notarised Chinese or English translation if the original is in neither language (NCU's published list).
Full official transcript including grade descriptions, GPAs and class rankings (NCU's published list).
Proof of nationality: passport photo page, or national identity document with photograph and English name, plus a Taiwan Alien Resident Certificate if applicable (NCU's published list).
Language proficiency certificate meeting the programme's minimum requirement (NCU's published list).
One or two recommendation letters submitted by the recommenders themselves through the online reference system (NCU's published list).
A recent close-up colour photograph, the online international student application declaration, and a bank statement showing at least USD 5,000 (NCU's published list).
selection_criteria: Applicants are selected primarily through the review of application data; additional written tests, phone or video interviews are performed according to each programme's policy (NCU).
Where an applicant's Chinese or English proficiency certificate falls below the minimum requirement, the department or graduate institute committee has the right to reject admission (NCU).
Second-year continued funding depends on passing the review of grades and performance by the school and the partner company (NTU's INTENSE terms).
Documents found to be fraudulent, forged, fabricated, altered or invalid lead to immediate cancellation of the application or the admission offer (NCU).
coverage: Tuition and miscellaneous fees: first year subsidised in full by the government (National Development Fund), second year subsidised on merit, for up to two years.
Other administrative costs covered by the government for up to two years.
A one-off air ticket to Taiwan.
A monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000, provided by the participating company for up to two years.
An internship allowance during off-campus internship courses, not lower than the minimum wage.
application_method: Apply online through the participating university's own admissions portal during that university's published window; MOE runs no central application.
At NCU: complete the online application form, have recommenders submit their letters through the online reference system, then upload every document before the deadline.
At NTUT: the 2027 Fall intake works to a student nomination deadline of 10 March 2027, with results announced in June 2027.
At NCU, an applicant may apply for up to three departments or graduate institutes, but may accept only one admission offer.
official.application_route: Direct to a participating university's approved INTENSE programme through that university's own online admissions portal - there is no MOE-wide application.
official.study_mode: Degree programme built on a two-year learning-and-internship plan
official.citizenship_residency: International students. MOE defines eligible candidates as international students who have completed their second or third year at an overseas university, or junior college graduates and bachelor's degree holders (the Chinese page also lists master's degree graduates). Some participating programmes restrict eligible nationalities, for example Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand at NCU.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme exists to recruit international students into degree programmes in Taiwan, followed by employment in Taiwan.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Key industry fields only: STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics), finance and semiconductors.
official.duration: Up to two years of funded study and internship, followed by employment with the participating company for a period matching the years of funding received
official.description: The Ministry of Education launched the International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program) for talents coming to Taiwan for study and employment after graduation, integrating resources from government, industry and universities to expand the recruitment of international superior industrial talents students and cultivate high-quality professionals with international mobility.
official.program_type: MOE specialised industry-academia class (International Industrial Talents Education Special Program) with a compulsory work obligation in Taiwan after graduation
official.english_requirement: MOE publishes no single English test score; each university sets its own. NCU publishes CEFR B1 or above for English-taught programmes (examples given: TOEFL iBT 42, IELTS 4, TOEIC 550, GEPT Intermediate), with exemption for applicants from English-speaking countries, and CEFR A2 or above (e.g. TOCFL Band A Level 2) for Chinese-taught programmes. NTU's INTENSE terms additionally require TOCFL Level A2 or above (listening and reading) for English-taught students and TOCFL Level B1 or above for Chinese-taught students in the second year.

not_confirmed: A programme-wide application deadline - none is published; each participating university sets its own per intake
The living allowance above the NT$10,000 minimum, which varies by partner company and is not published centrally
The complete document list for each individual programme, which lives in each university's admission guidelines
Any central IELTS/TOEFL score requirement issued by MOE
verification.notes: Award structure and the NT$10,000 minimum monthly allowance were verified on MOE's own INTENSE pages (English policy page dated 2025-12-23 and the Chinese plan page), and corroborated by two participating universities' own admissions pages (NCU, NTUT). The brief's stored official_source_url and application_link pointed to NTU's Overseas Compatriot and Mainland Chinese Students Advising Division, which does not host this programme.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not one scholarship but a national scheme delivered university by university, so the first job is picking the right partner university and programme rather than filling in a form. The money comes from two directions: the state pays your tuition, administrative costs and a one-way ticket, while the company you are matched with pays at least NT$10,000 a month plus an internship allowance at or above minimum wage. In exchange you contract to work in Taiwan for that company for as many years as you were funded, and the second year of tuition support is merit-based rather than automatic.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International students in STEM, finance or semiconductor-related fields who are willing to commit to working in Taiwan for a partner company after graduation.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist participating universities and programmes whose published nationality list includes yours and whose intake window is still open.
Check the language of instruction early and obtain a CEFR B1 (English-taught) or CEFR A2 (Chinese-taught) certificate from a test the university recognises.
Arrange notarised Chinese or English translations of your degree certificate and full transcripts before the window opens.
Line up one or two recommenders who can upload letters themselves through the university's online reference system.
Prepare the financial evidence NCU asks for (a bank statement showing at least USD 5,000) and a recent passport-style photograph.
Diarise the two annual rounds: Spring intake applications around October to December, Fall intake around January to March, checking each university's own dates.
common_rejection_risks: Your nationality is not on that programme's eligible list, which differs by university and even by department.
Late or incomplete submission: NCU explicitly refuses hard-copy, late and incomplete applications, and files cannot be added or replaced after the deadline.
Transcripts or degree certificates that are neither Chinese nor English, or translated by an agency not registered in the country of study.
A language certificate below the stated minimum, which gives the reviewing committee grounds to reject outright.
Losing second-year funding by failing the school's and partner company's grade and performance review, or missing the required TOCFL level.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published package covers tuition and miscellaneous fees (capped at NT$100,000 per year in NTU's version), administrative costs, a one-way ticket and a monthly allowance of at least NT$10,000. You still fund your own accommodation, insurance, internet, credit and thesis fees above the cap, plus return airfare, visa fees, document notarisation and authentication costs.
document_audit: Translations must be done and notarised by agencies registered in the country where you studied - a local translator is not enough.

Official certificates and transcripts must be verified by the ROC (Taiwan) embassy or representative office in or near the issuing country before the semester starts, or the admission offer is cancelled.
Recommendation letters are submitted by the referees through the online reference system; you cannot upload them yourself.
Each document goes into its own field as a single PDF (photograph as JPG), and nothing can be swapped after the deadline.
Applicants who are or were ROC nationals, or who hold Hong Kong or Macao permanent residence, must add renunciation and arrival-departure evidence.
alerts: The post-graduation work obligation in Taiwan is contractual and scales with the number of years of funding you accepted.
There is no central deadline: windows open and close at different times, so a closed university does not mean a closed scheme.
NTUT flags that admitting departments, quotas, funding amounts and eligibility criteria may change with the latest MOE and NTUT announcements.
Second-year tuition support is awarded on merit and depends on the partner company's review, so year one performance matters from day one.
Some programmes are still being adjusted: at least one participating university has temporarily suspended admissions for a particular specialisation.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the university's online form, get referees to submit through the reference system, then make one complete upload round before that university's cut-off - nothing can be added or replaced afterwards.

official.deadline_note: The published application period is 23 April to 15 May 2026, submitted through the International Degree Current Student System. That round has closed; NTU states that the scholarship renewal application takes place between April and May each year, so the next round is expected in the same April-May window but is not yet published.
official.application_cycle: Annual; the 2026 round ran 23 April to 15 May 2026, with renewal applications between April and May each year
official.status_note: The published application period was 23 April to 15 May 2026 and has closed. NTU states that renewal applications take place between April and May each year and that recipients should watch the OIA website and the International Degree Current Student System.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition fees of up to NTD 100,000 will be waived. This is exclusive of administrative fees, thesis advisor's fees, insurance, accommodation, internet service, credit fees and other such fees, which the recipients shall bear on their own.
benefits: Tuition waiver: tuition fees of up to NTD 100,000 are waived, exclusive of administrative fees, thesis advisor's fees, insurance, accommodation, internet service, credit fees and other such fees, which recipients bear themselves.
Monthly stipend provided by the advisor or the department, which may come with corresponding responsibilities as assigned: NTD 8,000 per month for master's students.
Monthly stipend for PhD students: NTD 10,000 per month for the College of Liberal Arts, Law, Social Science or Management, and NTD 15,000 per month for other colleges.
Renewable support: master's degree up to the 2nd year and doctoral degree up to the 4th year, subject to the annual review.
The Office of International Affairs is not responsible for the monthly stipend disbursement; the exact remittance date is determined by NTU's Accounting Office and the Cashier Division.
eligibility: Current international graduate student at NTU.
Master's students under the 2nd year; PhD students under the 4th year.
Available to currently-enrolled international degree students admitted to NTU in accordance with the Ministry of Education's Regulations for International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.
This does not include dual-degree students; NTU's scholarship FAQ confirms that students who came to NTU under a two-university agreement are not eligible.
requirements: Be a current international graduate student at NTU within the published year limits (master's under 2nd year, PhD under 4th year).
Secure an advisor or department willing to provide the monthly stipend, which may come with corresponding assigned responsibilities.
Submit past years' transcripts, or the Advisor Evaluation Form for graduate students who have no transcripts.
Submit the recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship and a curriculum vitae.
Renew the scholarship each year by re-applying between April and May and uploading the required documents for review.
documents: Past years' transcripts, or the Advisor Evaluation Form for graduate students who do not have transcripts.
Recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship.
Other beneficial materials, such as award records, proof of outstanding performance or publications.
selection_criteria: NTU's scholarship FAQ states that the decision is made by the review professors of the college to which the applicant belongs.
NTU's scholarship FAQ states that about half of applicants receive scholarships each year.
NTU's scholarship FAQ advises that documents with errors or omissions will certainly reduce the chance of an award.
Results are announced in the application system at the end of May.
coverage: Tuition waiver of up to NTD 100,000 from the university.
Monthly stipend provided by the advisor or the department: NTD 8,000 for master's students; NTD 10,000 or NTD 15,000 for PhD students depending on college.
The monthly stipend may come with corresponding responsibilities assigned by the advisor or department.
application_method: Submit the application through the International Degree Current Student System during the published application period.
Upload past years' transcripts or the Advisor Evaluation Form, the recommendation letter, the curriculum vitae and any other beneficial materials.
Renew each year by re-applying between April and May, following the instructions in the International Degree Current Student System.
official.application_route: Online through NTU's International Degree Current Student System during the annual April-May application period.
official.study_mode: Master's or doctoral degree study at NTU as a currently-enrolled international graduate student
official.citizenship_residency: International students admitted under the MOE Regulations for International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan; dual-degree students are excluded.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, but only for current international degree students already enrolled at NTU - prospective applicants cannot apply for this award.
official.duration: Master's degree up to the 2nd year; doctoral degree up to the 4th year
official.description: NTU's International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship supports current international graduate students through a matching structure: the university waives tuition of up to NTD 100,000 while the student's advisor or department provides a monthly stipend that may carry assigned responsibilities.
official.program_type: University merit scholarship with a matching-fund structure (NTU tuition waiver plus an advisor- or department-paid monthly stipend)

not_confirmed: English language requirement - none is published for this award
Travel, installation or one-off allowance - none is published
The 2027 application dates - not yet published
Any monthly stipend above the published minimums, which depends on the individual advisor or department
verification.notes: Award, amounts, documents and window were verified on NTU OIA's International Student Services scholarships page, which currently publishes a tuition waiver of up to NTD 100,000 plus monthly stipends of NTD 8,000 (master's) and NTD 10,000/15,000 (PhD by college). Selection-process detail comes from NTU OIA's scholarship FAQ. The OIA 'Scholarships for Current Students' hub cited in the brief is stale (last updated 2024/04/23) and the stored NTD 6,000/8,000 figures are superseded.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a matching-fund award for students already inside NTU: the university waives tuition of up to NTD 100,000, and your own advisor or department pays the monthly stipend of NTD 8,000 for master's students and NTD 10,000-15,000 for PhD students depending on college. Because the monthly money is tied to a professor's agreement, the real application step is winning a supervisor's commitment before the April-May window opens. About half of applicants succeed, and the decision rests with the professors of your own college.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled international master's or PhD students at NTU who already have, or can win, a supervisor's commitment to fund a monthly research-assistant salary.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure your advisor's or department's agreement to provide the monthly stipend before the April-May window opens - there is no central fund behind it.
Pull together past years' transcripts, or the Advisor Evaluation Form if you spent the year writing your thesis with no course records.
Ask your recommender early for the specific recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship rather than a generic letter.
Prepare a curriculum vitae and gather award records, performance evidence or publications as supporting material.
Keep a valid ARC (purpose of residence: study at NTU) and a Taiwanese postal bank account passbook cover ready to upload once awarded.
Re-apply every year between April and May - the award is not automatically renewed.
common_rejection_risks: No supervisor or department commitment, since the monthly stipend has no other funding source.
Submitting a blank or missing transcript after a thesis-only year instead of the Advisor Evaluation Form.
A generic recommendation letter instead of the named form for this scholarship.
Applying while holding another NTU or Taiwan government scholarship, where exclusivity rules apply.
Graduating, taking a leave of absence or withdrawing, which immediately invalidates the scholarship.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Recipients bear administrative fees, thesis advisor's fees, insurance, accommodation, internet service, credit fees and any tuition above the NTD 100,000 waiver cap. NTU's scholarship FAQ confirms that tuition and miscellaneous fees show as zero on the bill, but accommodation, insurance and internet charges must still be paid by the student.
document_audit: The recommendation letter must be the form specific to the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship.
If you have no transcript because you were writing your thesis, submit the Advisor Evaluation Form - a missing transcript is the classic failure point here.
Applications and renewals go through the International Degree Current Student System, not by email.
The Advisor Evaluation Form must be completed by your advisor, so ask early rather than in the final week of the window.
alerts: The 2026 window (23 April to 15 May 2026) is closed; the next round is only expected around April-May 2027 and is not yet published.

The Office of International Affairs does not pay the stipend: remittance depends on NTU's Accounting Office and the Cashier Division, and January and February payments can slip with the fiscal-year change and the Lunar New Year holiday.
Recipients must upload their ARC and bank details, plus the previous semester's transcript and the new semester's tuition payment receipt, for each renewal.
The monthly stipend may come with responsibilities assigned by the advisor or department - agree the workload before you rely on the income.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through the International Degree Current Student System during the April-May window; review is done by the professors of your college and results appear in the application system at the end of May.
